This fixture is independently compiled twice from ordinary TSX `pcbPath`: once with a single authored via, once with explicit colocated wire contacts around that via. No points are removed or routing geometry substituted. Both describe the same 3 mm TOP wire, 2 mm BOTTOM wire, two actual SMT pads, and emitted TOP-to-BOTTOM via on a four-layer board.

The repository's existing direct Core dependency resolves to 0.0.1930. The identical TSX was also compiled with published Core 0.0.2125: it retains the same three/five route points and the current checker again reports one error for compact encoding versus none for the contact-expanded control. Copper length in the comparison is measured from actual nonzero segments; the older compiler's `trace_length` field is not the comparison metric.

Current checks 0.0.247 rejects the compact input because its interior-via loop compares both neighboring wire coordinates against the via and requires differences below 0.01 mm. Nonzero wire-to-via and via-to-wire edges are valid authored geometry, so that requirement reports a false `misaligned_via` error. The snapshot draws the actual compiled copper and labels the actual public checker results.

Related open [#232](https://github.com/tscircuit/checks/pull/232) detects disconnected via transitions and physical layer-span mismatches while deliberately retaining the same coordinate-alignment requirement. It does not address this valid compact encoding. [#381](https://github.com/tscircuit/checks/pull/381) concerns onward copper at terminal via landings. Neither is a duplicate of this interior compact-route false rejection. Searches for compact and misaligned found no existing PR for this case.
